question: What is the primary purpose of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: To eliminate the need for community participation in health matters
options.B: To replace clinical bedside nursing with administrative duties
options.C: To secure permanent international funding for local hospitals
options.D: To provide a structured framework for addressing population health issues

explanation: The cycle gives health workers a systematic guide to identify and tackle public health problems logically. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is the community health planning process described as a cycle rather than a straight line?

options.A: Because interventions must be repeated every three months without fail
options.B: Because government policies force programs to restart annually
options.C: Because evaluation findings continuously feed back into new assessments
options.D: Because funding streams always expire at the end of every year

explanation: Health needs change over time, so evaluating outcomes naturally leads back to identifying new or persisting community needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which activity represents primary data collection during a community needs assessment?

options.A: Analyzing last year's outpatient morbidity registers
options.B: Reviewing national census reports in the public library
options.C: Conducting household surveys and focus group discussions

explanation: Primary data is collected firsthand directly from the community members through active engagement tools. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of relying exclusively on hospital attendance records for a community diagnosis?

options.A: It provides too much qualitative data that is difficult to analyze statistically
options.B: It is far too expensive compared to conducting large household surveys
options.C: It only reflects diseases that occurred more than ten years ago
options.D: It fails to capture health issues of people who cannot access formal health facilities

explanation: Facility registers miss individuals with barriers to care, leading to an incomplete picture of total community health needs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of priority setting in public health planning?

options.A: To comply with international donor requirements without local input
options.B: To select which health issue to address first given limited resources
options.C: To eliminate all identified community health problems permanently
options.D: To decide which healthcare workers will receive salary bonuses

explanation: Because resources are finite, priority setting helps health planners focus energy where intervention is most urgent and feasible. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: A community health team identifies five major health issues but has funding for only one program. Which criterion should carry the heaviest weight in their decision?

options.A: The availability of colorful promotional brochures for the launch
options.B: The personal preference of the local government chairperson
options.C: The magnitude and severity of the health problem combined with intervention feasibility
options.D: The speed at which international agencies can ship imported medications

explanation: Effective priority setting balances how many people are affected, how severe the impact is, and whether the team has the capacity to fix it. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the SMART objective-setting framework?
explanation: In health planning, objectives must be measurable so progress and outcomes can be accurately evaluated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why is community leader involvement crucial during the program design phase?

options.A: To secure local buy-in and ensure cultural appropriateness of planned activities
options.B: To shift all physical labor responsibilities away from professional nurses
options.C: To ensure that clinical staff do not need to write formal reports
options.D: To prevent the local government from auditing project expenditures

explanation: Involving community stakeholders early fosters trust and ensures interventions respect local customs and norms. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which category of resources includes community health extension workers and trained volunteers?
explanation: Personnel, staff, and volunteers constitute the human resource component of any health project. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is a primary danger of poor resource allocation during health planning?

options.A: Health workers will spend less time documenting patient interactions
options.B: Critical activities may stall midway due to shortages of supplies or personnel
options.C: International donors will automatically increase their annual funding grants
options.D: The community will immediately reject the program without giving feedback

explanation: Without proper budgeting and distribution, projects often run out of essential materials before reaching their objectives. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: What defines the implementation phase of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: Analyzing baseline survey data to write the initial community diagnosis
options.B: Conducting the final end-of-project summative evaluation
options.C: Putting the designed health plan into action through service delivery
options.D: Setting numerical targets and writing formal project proposals

explanation: Implementation is where planned activities are actively carried out in the target community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: Why is operational flexibility important during the implementation of a community health plan?

options.A: To adapt to unexpected challenges like weather disruptions or supply delays
options.B: To ensure that spending budgets can exceed approved limits indefinitely
options.C: To bypass community leaders when local opposition arises
options.D: To allow nurses to completely ignore original project objectives

explanation: Field realities often differ from desk plans, requiring teams to adjust methods without losing sight of overall goals. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring happens only after a project ends, while evaluation occurs daily
options.B: Monitoring focuses strictly on financial audits, while evaluation looks at drugs
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing activity tracking, while evaluation measures overall outcomes and impact
options.D: Monitoring is done by community members, while evaluation is done by politicians

explanation: Monitoring tracks daily progress, whereas evaluation assesses whether the long-term goals were successfully achieved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: When is a formative evaluation typically carried out during a health program?

options.A: Only when writing the very final funding report for international donors
options.B: Years after the program has completely shut down and closed
options.C: Before any data collection or community diagnosis has started
options.D: During the implementation phase to allow for mid-course corrections

explanation: Formative evaluation happens while the program is running so adjustments can be made immediately if needed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced in Nigerian community health planning?

options.A: Unlimited and surplus government health funding
options.B: Inaccurate or delayed facility data reporting
options.D: Infrastructural deficits like poor road networks

explanation: Funding in public healthcare is rarely surplus; financial scarcity is one of the most prominent challenges in the sector. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: How can public health nurses help mitigate data reporting issues at primary healthcare facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: By inflating monthly attendance figures to please political officeholders
options.B: By relying entirely on oral memory rather than written registers
options.C: By stopping all data collection until international consultants arrive
options.D: By advocating for and adopting reliable digital or mobile health data tools

explanation: Modern digital tools reduce paper-based errors and improve the accuracy and speed of health data reporting. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)
